model_annotations.Bulgarian: The table presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates (10% to 80%) for two methods, DLP and a baseline, using the WANDA language model. The data is visualized as a 9x7 matrix with bold and non-bold highlights, with the bold cells indicating the best performance result. The headings of the table are method and percentage, with the values beneath them representing the perplexity scores for both per-output and per-layer. The table also includes a column for sparsity rates and another for comparison to the baseline method. There are no graphical elements accompanying the table.

DLP: Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
mete Data for Figure 5:
- Title: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, using Wanda.
- Purpose: The graph compares the performance of DLP in reducing per-output and per-layer perplexity at various sparsity rates.
- x-axis: Sparsity rates (%), labeled with values from 10% to 80%.
- y1-axis (Per-Output): Represents per-output perplexity values, with unit not specified but inferred to be perplexity.
- y2-axis (Per-Layer): Represents per-layer perplexity values, with unit not specified but inferred to be perplexity.
- Bars: Each sparsity rate has two bars (black and orange), representing per-output and per-layer perplexity values, respectively.
- Remarks: The values are logarithmic due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The bolded text indicates the best performance result.
